document.title: Expected review outcomes for every eval case
document.summary: Adds shared review criteria and one `expected.md` per eval case, then tightens each `case.json` to match those outcomes.
document.why: [#117](source:s1) asks for a written expected outcome per eval case, because the current gates pass every run and do not steer the skill.

sources.title: Manually review eval cases and write expected outcomes
sources.gist: Write an expected outcome per case, then fold it into case.json and iterate on the skill.

sources.label: PR #118
sources.gist: Phase 1 of #117, drafted by an agent for Máté's review.

lookFor: [#117](source:s1) says notes go in issue comments or straight into `case.json`. The change puts them in `expected.md` files next to each case, so they stay versioned with the expects.

Breaking: the new gates fail most past reviews. Re-scoring the 60 reviews from the six baseline runs gives 18 passes, against 60 with the old gates. A merge to `main` runs the graded suite and will likely go red.

parts.name: Expected outcomes
parts.summary: Review criteria and one written outcome per case.

parts.name: Gating expects
parts.summary: The parts of each outcome that the harness can check, written into `case.json`.

groups.title: Shared review criteria
groups.why: Every case is judged the same way, as [#117](source:s1) asks.
groups.summary: `eval/review-criteria.md` lists the grouping, source-comparison, and lookFor rules, and the section template each `expected.md` follows.

groups.title: Expected outcome per case
groups.why: [#117](source:s1) asks what a good review of each case looks like, so misses can be told apart from expects that ask too much.
groups.summary: Each `expected.md` names the groups, the must-state and good-to-state claims, the mistakes to avoid, and what the six baseline runs did.
lookFor: Every must-state claim was checked against the code at head. The riskiest ones: `server.sh` deleting `.env.local` (cigster-99), what a matching comment pin means (comprehende-47), and the dropped Refresh and coverage on mobile (comprehende-59).
comprehende-59 leaves the document why as an open question. The PR says what changes, not why.

groups.title: Tighter case.json expects
groups.why: [#117](source:s1) phase 2 starts by folding the outcomes into the expects. This part can be dropped and taken later with the skill change.
groups.summary: Each `case.json` gets tighter `parts` ranges, `together` pairs that keep tests with their code, fuller `mechanicalPaths`, and the must-state claims.
lookFor: The `together` pairs for tests encode a rule the skill does not state yet. They fail every past run of comprehende-57, comprehende-59, and comprehende-67.
comprehende-59 loses its `why` gate. That is the only gate this change loosens.

commits.subject: Fold expected outcomes into eval case expects
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Tighten parts ranges, add together pairs that keep tests with their code,
widen mechanicalPaths to every copy, and replace easy claims with the
must-state claims from each expected.md. Re-scoring the 60 reviews from
the six baseline runs: 18 pass the new gates, 60 passed the old ones.

Co-authored-by: doglotteger <doglotteger@gmail.com>
